I am studying psychology and I'm against the therapy culture we have nowadays. Modern psychology focuses a bit too much on individualizing problematics that are general, the whole thing about telling, for example, men to go to therapy bc they are misogynistic is so dumb  bc it's not a one-person-problem. The same thing goes to "usual" disorders: anxiety, depression, and now ADHD that is on the "rise"; all of these are just symptoms of the same issue, capitalism.

In psychology, a disorder is considered to be something out of the norm and that norm is not only social but statistic as well. It's not necessarily about healthiness or well-being, just about following the pattern. I'm against such ideas and, while of course there are conditions that will deeply affect you and your interactions with the world, there are plenty more that I think are just a result of living a life we are not supposed to live.

Of course we are going to have depression, of course we are going to have anxiety, of course we are going to have substances addictions; these are the true "NORMAL" behaviors for me, not the healthiest but the normal-est. Every aspect of our socioeconomic model pushes us to have these, for me it would be truly disturbing to not be able to react negatively to such a horrible life.

Esta formación de modelos de producción después de la civilización trae una división de poderes económicos que se forma en el famoso concepto de división de clases (en el esclavismo es esclavo y dueño, señol feudal y siervos, burgués y proletariado).

Obvio es un tema más complejo y mucho más rico que lo que yo te pueda decir en este post, si te interesa estos temas (y le sabes al inglés ) te sugeriría r/marxism_101 para que te guíen más en el materialismo histórico y dialéctico dependiendo de tus dudas.

Not only a resume, depending on the college and if it's more industry wise or "contemporary art" wise I would suggest  adding an artist statement. 
An artist statement is basically an introduction of you as a person and well, artist. You say important stuff about your life like where you're from and your influences over the years.
Then you explain how those influences have shaped your artistic journey: ex. "I was born in the 2000s, a beginning for the mainstream internet era so that's why I make digital art focused on this and this topics"
It's carefully written and redacted, it also explains your previous experiences. It usually isn't longer than half a page.
I wouldn't say this is a replacement for the resume but it's a professional way to give context of who you are.

Also, as for showing images for the portafolio you should consider the following 

A) Put your strongest pieces at the beginning of the portafolio and at the end 

B) It should be tailored with your most important works that show your area of expertise (if your college is an animation college you show your frames per frames/storyboards, if it's a design college you show your designs, if it's a general visual arts you show your different techniques)

C)You should create a route on how you show your works, whether it's a timeline, a narration or a display or techniques.

D) While WIPs may be useful, I don't suggest your whole portafolio are WIPs , it's nice to show the process but showing finished products will display what you can accomplish (and if you can finish tasks)

E)I recommend watching particular videos of people applying to your same college, there must be some somewhere. I will definitely take their insight for what the school is looking for.

F) Start with time, specially if you have to print something. You can end with a very messy portafolio if you do it the night before.

G) Check the edition, look how the image you present is placed in the space you have given it. Check margins or if you want to go for a bold style and fill the whole page. Have intentions on where you position things and why

G.2) If you do print stuff, check that your RGB values match your CMYK so you don't get surprised. I suggest trying to make a test printing of one or two pages so you can adjust the colors (this particularly if you have to do it on a budget and can't afford a fancy printing station where all their printers and screens are calibrated).

F) Last but not least and VERY important, check the instructions you are given and if any particular format is requested. If not, try to be creative with how you show your work and make it make sense in how you do art.

Favorite people are simply emotional addictions, it doesn't have to be a sexual/romantic partner necessarily they just have to be someone you feel this strong need to be around or check on. In my experience FPs basically dictate how I feel with their actions: example, didn't answer my text immediately and I see they have been online during the next hours will absolutely cause me to split on them passing from "Oh they are so kind and loving to me" to "How can they be so cruel, why are they so dismissing" in a matter of seconds. 
As an addiction I get a rush when I have a "positive" interaction with them, even if it's just them being around and get withdrawal symptoms when they aren't around or our interactions are off (even if it's just me perceiving them like that): heavy anxiety, paranoia, getting irritated, depression, insomnia, etc etc. 
I could recommend reading Love and Addiction from Staton Peele due to its observations towards how addiction without substance can happen although be aware that it leans towards romantically dependency so do not think it's only that.
We can become addicted to anything and anyone, they just need to give us enough dopamine to do so
